title: Terminal open must not navigate to external URLs or after the terminal stops, and must stay lazy
answers: Is terminal open safe against external redirect?
Why does open not download file contents?
body:
Terminal navigation to PostHog pages is guarded in two places:
- `PosthogFilesystem.navigationUrl` (posthogFilesystem.ts) only returns internal hrefs: must start with `/`, not `//`, and contain no backslash, control chars or whitespace. Otherwise it throws 'no PostHog page'. Tests cover https:, //, /\, javascript:, newline. Keep this check on any new navigation path, since hrefs come from stored file entries.
- `PosthogCommands.execute('open')` re-checks `this.signal.aborted` after the async resolve and before calling `navigate`, so a stopped terminal never navigates.
- Resolution walks nodes with `loadChildren` per folder only, and uses stored identity (`references`, `fileSystemTypes[type].href`), never `notebooksRetrieve`/`fileSystemRetrieve`. Preserve lazy loading; tests assert those are not called.
Navigation is injected as a callback (terminalLogic passes `router.actions.push`), keeping PosthogCommands testable.

Node resolution walks folders with loadChildren and uses stored identity (references, fileSystemTypes[type].href), never calling notebooksRetrieve or fileSystemRetrieve, to preserve lazy loading. Tests must assert lazy-loading methods are not called during navigation resolution. This invariant prevents injection attacks and ensures lazy resolution in terminal open/navigation code in frontend/src/scenes/terminal/posthogFilesystem.ts, posthogCommands.ts, and terminalLogic.ts.
